title: Theorem 10.31.11
text: Theorem 10.31.11 . 4AC0DDA39172 Let $u_ j,u\in \mathcal E_\varphi $, with $u_ j\to u$ in $L^1(X)$. If \[  \int _ X|u_ j-u|\, \mu _{u_ j}\longrightarrow 0,  \] then $u_ j\to u$ in capacity. Moreover, after passing to a subsequence, $P_\theta (\inf _{k\geq j}u_ k)$ belongs to $\mathcal E_\varphi $ for every $j$. Proof. Start with any subsequence and extract a further subsequence along which the integrals in the hypothesis are at most $2^{-j}$ and $u_ j\to u$ almost everywhere for smooth volume. The envelope identity and Hartogs' lemma give a uniform bound $u_ j,u\leq \varphi +C$. For $N\geq j$ let $p_{j,N}=P_\theta (u_ j,\ldots ,u_ N)$. Partitioning the contact set according to the first obstacle touched gives 706A43A92BE8 10.31.12 \begin{equation}  \int _ X|p_{j,N}-u|\, \mu _{p_{j,N}}\leq 2^{1-j}. \end{equation} Apply proposition 10.31.8 with $w=u$, in its one-sided form. It bounds $\sup _ Xp_{j,N}$ from below, independently of $N$. Consequently the decreasing sequence has a limit \[  p_ j=P_\theta \left(\inf _{k\geq j}u_ k\right)  \] that is not identically $-\infty $, and the same proposition puts $p_ j$ in $\mathcal E_\varphi $. The increasing sequence $p_ j$ has a regularized limit $p$, which belongs to $\mathcal E_\varphi $ by upward stability, since $p_1\leq p\leq u\preceq \varphi $. The inequality $p\leq u$ follows from the almost-everywhere convergence of the extracted sequence. Both $p_{j,N}\downarrow p_ j$ and $p_ j\uparrow p$ hold in capacity by lemma 5.29.19 , since $p_1\not\equiv -\infty $ is a common lower bound. Apply lemma 13.14.8 to ( 10.31.12 ), with the bounded weights $\min (1,|p_{j,N}-u|)$ and then $\min (1,|p_ j-u|)$. These weights converge in capacity: discard the deep sublevel sets of $p_1$ and $u$, and use that $\min (1,|x-y|)$ is Lipschitz on finite values. The result is \[  \int _ X\min (1,|p-u|)\, \mu _ p=0.  \] Hence $\mu _ p(\{ p<u\} )=0$, and zero domination gives $p=u$. The upper envelopes $(\sup _{k\geq j}u_ k)^*$ decrease to $u$. Squeezing the extracted $u_ j$ between these envelopes and $p_ j$ proves convergence in capacity. Since the initial subsequence was arbitrary, the conclusion holds for the original sequence. $\square$

title: Lemma 10.31.14
text: Lemma 10.31.14 . E0503BA0806A Let $u\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ satisfy $u\sim V$ and $u\leq V$. Let $\chi :\mathbb R_{\leq 0}\to \mathbb R_{\leq 0}$ be increasing and concave, with $\chi (0)=0$ and $\chi '\geq 1$, and assume that $\chi $ is $C^{1,1}$ on compact intervals. Set \[  b=V+\chi (u-V),\qquad p=P_\theta (b),  \] where the obstacle $b$ is defined off the pole set of $V$ and is set equal to $-\infty $ on that set. Then $p\sim V$ and \[  \mu _ p\leq \mathbf1_{\{ p=b\} }\chi '(u-V)^ n\mu _ u.  \] The measures and contact sets in this inequality may be restricted to the complement of the pole set of any fixed strict analytic barrier for $\theta $, that is, of any $\rho \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ with analytic singularities such that $\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}\rho \geq a\omega $ for some $a>0$. Proof. The difference $u-V$ is bounded, so $V-C\leq b\leq u\leq V$ for some constant $C$. Hence $p\sim V$. The obstacle is quasi-continuous: away from sets of arbitrarily small capacity, $u$ and $V$ are finite and continuous, and their difference has a fixed bounded range. The general contact theorem theorem 15.8.6 therefore applies. Choose a strict analytic barrier $\rho $ and translate it so that $\rho \leq V$; put $\Omega =X\setminus \{ \rho =-\infty \} $. On this open set $u$, $V$ and $p$ are locally bounded. Let $\tau =\chi ^{-1}$; then $\tau $ is convex and $0<\tau '\leq 1$. By lemma 5.28.13 , the function \[  w=V+\tau (p-V)  \] is $\theta $-plurisubharmonic on $\Omega $ and satisfies \[  \mathrm{MA}_\theta (w)\geq \tau '(p-V)^ n\mu _ p.  \] Since $p\leq w\leq V$ on $\Omega $, the removability lemma lemma 5.24.7 extends $w$ across the analytic set $X\setminus \Omega $, preserving its smooth lower curvature bound. The inequality $p\leq b$ implies $w\leq u$, with equality on $D=\{ p=b\} $. Ordered contact gives \[  \mathbf1_ D\tau '(p-V)^ n\mu _ p \leq \mathbf1_ D\mathrm{MA}_\theta (w) \leq \mathbf1_ D\mu _ u.  \] On $D$ the derivative $\tau '(p-V)$ equals $1/\chi '(u-V)$. Together with contact support for $p$, this proves the claim on $\Omega $. The analytic set $X\setminus \Omega $ is not charged by the non-pluripolar measures involved. $\square$

title: 10.31.24 Relative projection and supersolutions
text:
To pass from the minimal class to the reference $\varphi $, we project a solution $z\in \mathcal E_ V$ onto $\mathcal E_\varphi $. The projection is the increasing limit $P_	heta [\varphi ](z)$ of the rooftops $P_	heta (\varphi +C,z)$ as $C	o \infty $, in the notation of lemma 13.19.4 . The small stretches of lemma 13.20.1 first show that the rooftop $P_	heta (\varphi ,z)$ is not identically $-\infty $ and has the full upper volume of $\varphi $. Contact support then bounds the measure of the projection by the measure of $z$ on the set where the two coincide. The argument uses only that the reference of $z$ lies above $\varphi $, so we formulate it for an arbitrary ordinary model above $\varphi $; this will also allow the reference to vary. Let $\eta \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$ satisfy $P_	heta [\eta ]=\eta \geq \varphi $, and write $\mathcal E_\eta =\mathcal E_{\mathrm{env}}(X,	heta ,\eta )$. Proposition 10.31.25 . 4F5454D09F78 For every $z\in \mathcal E_\eta $, the rooftop $P_	heta (\varphi ,z)$ is not identically $-\infty $ and belongs to $\mathcal E_\varphi $. Proof. First suppose $z\leq \eta $; recall also that $\varphi \leq \eta \leq 0$. For $b>1$ sufficiently close to one, lemma 13.20.1 gives \[  h_ b=Q_ b(\varphi ,\eta )\leq \varphi ,  \] which is not identically $-\infty $. Set $a=1-b^{-1}$. The stretching lemma lemma 16.28.63 , now applied in $\mathcal E_\eta $, gives $z_{1/a}=Q_{1/a}(z,\eta )\in \mathcal E_\eta $. The potential \[  k_ a=a z_{1/a}+(1-a)h_ b  \] lies below both $\varphi $ and $z$. Indeed, $z_{1/a}\leq \eta $ and $(1-a)h_ b+a\eta \leq \varphi $ give the first bound, while $h_ b\leq \eta $ and $a z_{1/a}+(1-a)\eta \leq z$ give the second. Thus $p=P_	heta (\varphi ,z)$ is not identically $-\infty $. Volume addition and monotonicity give \[  (1-a)^ n\overline{\operatorname {vol}}_	heta (h_ b) \leq \overline{\operatorname {vol}}_	heta (k_ a) \leq \overline{\operatorname {vol}}_	heta (p) \leq \overline{\operatorname {vol}}_	heta (\varphi ).  \] As $b\downarrow 1$, we have $a\downarrow 0$, and the first term tends to the last by lemma 13.20.1 . The upper volumes of $p$ and $\varphi $ are therefore equal. Since $p\leq \varphi $, theorem 13.18.5 gives $p\in \mathcal E_\varphi $. title: Proposition 10.31.25
text: Proposition 10.31.25 . 4F5454D09F78 For every $z\in \mathcal E_\eta $, the rooftop $P_\theta (\varphi ,z)$ is not identically $-\infty $ and belongs to $\mathcal E_\varphi $. Proof. For $b>1$ sufficiently close to one, lemma 13.20.1 gives \[  h_ b=Q_ b(\varphi ,\eta )\leq \varphi ,  \] which is not identically $-\infty $. Set $a=1-b^{-1}$. The stretching lemma lemma 16.28.63 , now applied in $\mathcal E_\eta $, gives $z_{1/a}=Q_{1/a}(z,\eta )\in \mathcal E_\eta $. title: 10.31.29 Varying model references
text:
We now let the reference vary. Recall from definition 13.22.1 the comparison \[  d_	heta (u,v)=2\, \overline{\operatorname {vol}}_	heta (\max (u,v)) -\overline{\operatorname {vol}}_	heta (u)-\overline{\operatorname {vol}}_	heta (v)  \] and, for $\delta >0$, the set $\mathcal M_\delta (	heta )$ of ordinary models $u=P_	heta [u]$ with $\underline{\operatorname {vol}}_	heta (u)\geq \delta $. For models $\varphi _ j	o \varphi $ in this comparison, theorem 13.23.3 provides increasing lower models whose upper volumes approach that of $\varphi $. Projecting finite families of potentials onto these lower models makes their rooftops comparable. To keep the limit in the relative class of $\varphi $, domination of the measures is needed only where the potentials lie below one fixed member of that class; domination on all of $X$ gives, in addition, convergence in capacity and convergence of the measures. Theorem 10.31.30 . 558CBE100687 Let $\varphi _ j,\varphi \in \mathcal M_\delta (	heta )$ for some $\delta >0$, with $d_	heta (\varphi _ j,\varphi )	o 0$. Suppose $u_ j\in \mathcal E_{\varphi _ j}$, $u_ j	o u\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )$ in $L^1(X)$, and $\chi \in \mathcal E_\varphi $. If one finite non-pluripolar measure $
u $ satisfies \[  \mathbf1_{\{ u_ j\leq \chi \} }\mu _{u_ j}\leq 
u ,  \] then $u\in \mathcal E_\varphi $. Moreover, after extraction and relabeling, the potentials \[  \psi _ j=P_	heta \left(\inf _{l\geq j}\varphi _ light),\qquad h_ j=P_	heta \left(\inf _{l\geq j}u_ light)  \] satisfy $\psi _ j\in \mathcal M_{\delta /2}(	heta )$ and $h_ j\in \mathcal E_{\psi _ j}$. If $\mu _{u_ j}\leq 
u $ on $X$, the original sequence converges to $u$ in capacity and $\mu _{u_ j}ightharpoonup \mu _ u$. Proof. We first construct the lower models $\psi _ j$, then a common lower bound for rooftops of the $u_ l$ in the classes $\mathcal E_{\psi _ j}$, and finally treat domination on all of $X$. By Hartogs' lemma, $u_ j$, $u$ and $\chi $ have a common upper bound; translate them to be nonpositive. The envelope identity then gives $u_ j\leq \varphi _ j$. Since $\varphi _ j	o \varphi $ in $L^1$ by proposition 13.22.4 , it follows that $u\leq \varphi $. Put $\Lambda =
u +\mu _\chi $. Using lemma 5.44.2 , extract a subsequence along which $u_ j	o u$ almost everywhere for smooth volume and \[  I_ j:=\int _ X|\mathrm{e}^{u_ j}-\mathrm{e}^ u|\, \mathrm{d}\Lambda \leq 2^{-j}.  \] Apply theorem 13.23.3 to extract further, keeping these estimates, and obtain increasing models $w_ j\leq \varphi _ j,\varphi $ with lower volume at least $\delta /2$ and $d_	heta (w_ j,\varphi )	o 0$. For $l\geq j$ we have $w_ j\leq w_ l\leq \varphi _ l$. Hence $\psi _ j$ is not identically $-\infty $, and \[  w_ j\leq \psi _ j\leq \varphi .  \] The upper bound follows by passing to the $L^1$ limit in $\psi _ j\leq \varphi _ l$ as $l	o \infty $. Monotonicity of the ordinary envelope gives $P_	heta [\psi _ j]\leq \varphi _ l$ for all $l\geq j$, so $\psi _ j$ is an ordinary model. It increases with $j$, has lower volume at least $\delta /2$, and 2A2692F560B3 10.31.31  egin{equation}  \overline{\operatorname {vol}}_	heta (\psi _ j) \longrightarrow \overline{\operatorname {vol}}_	heta (\varphi ). \end{equation} Set $g_ j=P_	heta [\psi _ j](\chi )$. Proposition 10.31.26 , with $(\varphi ,\eta )$ replaced by $(\psi _ j,\varphi )$, gives $g_ j\in \mathcal E_{\psi _ j}$, $g_ j\leq \chi $ and $\mu _{g_ j}\leq \mu _\chi $. Moreover $g_ j$ increases with $j$. For $N\geq j$, consider \[  q_{j,N}=P_	heta (g_ j,u_ j,\ldots ,u_ N).  \] For each $l\geq j$, the projection $P_	heta [\psi _ j](u_ l)$ belongs to $\mathcal E_{\psi _ j}$ by the same proposition, now with upper reference $\varphi _ l$. The finite rooftop of these projections and $g_ j$ lies below $q_{j,N}$. Since $q_{j,N}\leq g_ j$, the finite-rooftop proposition and upward stability give $q_{j,N}\in \mathcal E_{\psi _ j}$, and hence $\mu _{q_{j,N}}(X)\geq \delta /2$. Partition the contact set of $q_{j,N}$ into disjoint pieces, one for each obstacle. On a piece where $q_{j,N}=u_ l$, we have $u_ l\leq g_ j\leq \chi $, so the hypothesis bounds the measure there by $
u $. On the piece where $q_{j,N}=g_ j$, the measure is bounded by $\mu _{g_ j}\leq \mu _\chi $. Consequently $\mu _{q_{j,N}}\leq \Lambda $. Put $F_ j=\min (\mathrm{e}^ u,\mathrm{e}^{g_ j})$. On the $u_ l$ piece, \[  |\mathrm{e}^{q_{j,N}}-F_ j|\leq |\mathrm{e}^{u_ l}-\mathrm{e}^ u|.  \] On the $g_ j$ piece, $g_ j=q_{j,N}\leq u_ N$, so the error is $(\mathrm{e}^{g_ j}-\mathrm{e}^ u)_+\leq |\mathrm{e}^{u_ N}-\mathrm{e}^ u|$. The $u_ N$ piece and the $g_ j$ piece are controlled by the two summands $
u $ and $\mu _\chi $ of $\Lambda $, so together they contribute at most $I_ N$. Thus 4D376181A695 10.31.32  egin{equation}  \int _ X|\mathrm{e}^{q_{j,N}}-F_ j|\, \mu _{q_{j,N}} \leq \sum _{l=j}^ N I_ l\leq 2^{1-j}. \end{equation} Since $F_ j\geq F_1>0$ outside a pluripolar set, we may choose $\epsilon >0$ with $\Lambda (\{ F_1\leq \epsilon \} )<\delta /4$. Hence the decreasing limit $q_ j$ as $N	o \infty $ is not identically $-\infty $. Applying theorem 10.31.5 in the fixed class $\mathcal E_{\psi _ j}$, with dominating measure $\Lambda $, gives $q_ j\in \mathcal E_{\psi _ j}$. Now \[  q_ j\leq h_ j\leq \psi _ j,  \] so $h_ j\in \mathcal E_{\psi _ j}$ by upward stability. We discard the finitely many earlier indices. Since $h_ j\leq u\leq \varphi $, monotonicity and ( 10.31.31 ) show that $u$ and $\varphi $ have the same upper volume, and theorem 13.18.5 gives $u\in \mathcal E_\varphi $. Suppose now that $\mu _{u_ j}\leq 
u $ on $X$. The finite rooftops $p_{j,N}=P_	heta (u_ j,\ldots ,u_ N)$ are not identically $-\infty $, since they lie above $h_ j$. Partitioning their contact sets gives \[  \mu _{p_{j,N}}\leq 
u ,\qquad \int _ X|\mathrm{e}^{p_{j,N}}-\mathrm{e}^ u|\, \mu _{p_{j,N}}\leq 2^{1-j}.  \] For fixed $j$, they decrease to $h_ j$ as $N	o \infty $. These lower envelopes increase to a regularized limit $h\leq u\leq \varphi $, and their upper volumes tend to that of $\varphi $; hence $h\in \mathcal E_\varphi $. Both monotone limits hold in capacity by lemma 5.29.19 . Applying lemma 13.14.8 twice gives \[  \int _ X|\mathrm{e}^ h-\mathrm{e}^ u|\, \mu _ h=0.  \] Hence $\mu _ h(\{ h<u\} )=0$, and zero domination gives $h=u$. The upper envelopes $(\sup _{k\geq j}u_ k)^*$ decrease to $u$ by Hartogs' lemma and the almost-everywhere convergence, and squeezing gives convergence in capacity. Finally, \[  \mu _{u_ j}(\{ u_ j\leq -T\} )\leq 
u (\{ h_1\leq -T\} )\longrightarrow 0  \] uniformly in $j$, and the tail criterion theorem 13.15.23 gives weak convergence of the measures. Since the extraction can start from any subsequence, both conclusions hold for the original sequence. $\square$

title: 10.31.33 Weighted measure addition
text: Given $u,v\in \mathcal E_\varphi $ and $\lambda >0$, we look for $a\in \mathcal E_\varphi $ with $\mu _ a=\mathrm{e}^{\lambda (a-u)}\mu _ u+\mathrm{e}^{\lambda (a-v)}\mu _ v$. This weighted addition is used in subsection 10.31.43 to enlarge the weighted measure of a supersolution. The measure $\mathrm{e}^{-\lambda u}\mu _ u+\mathrm{e}^{-\lambda v}\mu _ v$ can have infinite mass, so we approximate the inputs while keeping a common lower bound in $\mathcal E_\varphi $ for the approximate solutions. This bound gives convergence in capacity, even when the approximate solutions have different ordinary types, and localizes the limiting equation away from deep sublevel sets. Exponentially weighted measures are defined off the pole sets and assigned zero mass there. Lemma 10.31.34 . 68A4962EA99D Let $a_ j\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ have a common upper bound and converge in $L^1(X)$ to $a\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ with $a\preceq \varphi $. Suppose there is $h\in \mathcal E_\varphi $ such that $h\leq a_ j$ for every $j$. If, for some $\lambda >0$, \[  \int _ X|a_ j-a|\mathrm{e}^{\lambda a}\, \mu _{a_ j}\longrightarrow 0,  \] then $a\in \mathcal E_\varphi $ and $a_ j\to a$ in capacity. Proof. By lemma 5.24.3 , the lower bound passes to the limit, so $h\leq a\preceq \varphi $, and upward stability gives $a\in \mathcal E_\varphi $. Start with any subsequence and extract a further one along which the integrals in the hypothesis are at most $2^{-j}$ and $a_ j\to a$ almost everywhere for smooth volume. The finite rooftops \[  p_{j,N}=P_\theta (a_ j,\ldots ,a_ N)  \] are not identically $-\infty $ because $h$ is a competitor. Partitioning their contact sets according to the first obstacle touched gives \[  \int _ X\min (1,|p_{j,N}-a|)\mathrm{e}^{\lambda a}\, \mu _{p_{j,N}} \leq \sum _{k=j}^ N\int _ X|a_ k-a|\mathrm{e}^{\lambda a}\, \mu _{a_ k} \leq 2^{1-j}.  \] No relative-class assertion about these finite rooftops is needed. Their decreasing limits $p_ j=P_\theta (\inf _{k\geq j}a_ k)$ are at least $h$, and the almost-everywhere convergence gives $p_ j\leq a$. Hence the $p_ j$ and their increasing regularized limit $p$ lie in $\mathcal E_\varphi $. The limits in $N$ and then in $j$ hold in capacity by lemma 5.29.19 , since $h$ is a common lower bound. Apply the weighted lower semicontinuity lemma 13.14.8 twice, to the bounded weights $\min (1,|p_{j,N}-a|)\mathrm{e}^{\lambda a}$ and their limits. These weights converge in capacity: discard deep sublevel sets of $h$ and $a$, and use continuity on the remaining finite ranges. We obtain \[  \int _ X\min (1,|p-a|)\mathrm{e}^{\lambda a}\, \mu _ p=0.  \] The exponential is positive off a pluripolar set, which $\mu _ p$ does not charge. Hence $\mu _ p(\{ p<a\} )=0$, and zero domination gives $p=a$. The upper envelopes $(\sup _{k\geq j}a_ k)^*$ decrease to $a$, and squeezing proves convergence in capacity along this subsequence. Since the initial subsequence was arbitrary, the convergence holds for the original sequence. $\square$ The next lemma treats exponent one; the general exponent in theorem 10.31.38 follows by rescaling the background and the potentials. Lemma 10.31.35 . F92458E62F62 Let $u,v,\sigma \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ be nonpositive, with $u,v\preceq \varphi $, and let $t_ j\uparrow \infty $. Each of the sequences $u_ j$, $v_ j$ is either constant, equal to $u$, respectively $v$, for every $j$, or given by the truncations \[  u_ j=\max (u,\sigma -t_ j),\qquad v_ j=\max (v,\sigma -t_ j).  \] Suppose that the Monge–Ampère masses of the $u_ j$ and $v_ j$ are uniformly bounded. Fix $h\in \mathcal E_\varphi $ and let $a_ j\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ satisfy \[  \mu _{a_ j}=\mathrm{e}^{a_ j-u_ j}\mu _{u_ j}+\mathrm{e}^{a_ j-v_ j}\mu _{v_ j}, \qquad h\leq a_ j\leq \min (u_ j,v_ j).  \] If $a_ j\to a$ in $L^1(X)$, then $a\in \mathcal E_\varphi $, the convergence holds in capacity, and \[  a\leq \min (u,v),\qquad \mu _ a=\mathrm{e}^{a-u}\mu _ u+\mathrm{e}^{a-v}\mu _ v.  \] The measure on the right is finite, even when $\mathrm{e}^{-u}\mu _ u+\mathrm{e}^{-v}\mu _ v$ has infinite total mass. Proof. Since $u_ j$ and $v_ j$ decrease to $u$ and $v$, the bounds give $h\leq a\leq \min (u,v)\preceq \varphi $, so $a\in \mathcal E_\varphi $. After discarding finitely many indices we may assume $t_ j\geq 0$, so all potentials $a_ j,a$ are nonpositive. Let $E_ j$ be the intersection of the sets $\{ u>\sigma -t_ j\} $ and $\{ v>\sigma -t_ j\} $, taken only for those inputs that are truncated; a constant sequence imposes no condition. On $E_ j$, locality gives $\mu _{u_ j}=\mu _ u$ and $\mu _{v_ j}=\mu _ v$. Since $a,a_ j\leq u_ j,v_ j$, we have \[  \mathrm{e}^ a\mu _{a_ j} \leq \mathrm{e}^{(a+a_ j)/2}(\mu _{u_ j}+\mu _{v_ j}).  \] If $x\notin E_ j$, then one truncated input and its truncation are at most $-t_ j$ at $x$, so $a_ j(x),a(x)\leq -t_ j$. The limiting right-hand side is at most $\mu _ u+\mu _ v$, because $a\leq u,v$. Both sides ignore the pole set of $h$, so the cutoff identities prove the global equation and the finiteness of its right-hand side. $\square$

title: Lemma 10.31.34
text: Lemma 10.31.34 . 68A4962EA99D Let $a_ j\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ have a common upper bound and converge in $L^1(X)$ to $a\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )$ with $a\preceq \varphi $. Suppose there is $h\in \mathcal E_\varphi $ such that $h\leq a_ j$ for every $j$. If, for some $\lambda >0$, \[  \int _ X|a_ j-a|\mathrm{e}^{\lambda a}\, \mu _{a_ j}\longrightarrow 0,  \] then $a\in \mathcal E_\varphi $ and $a_ j\to a$ in capacity. Proof. By lemma 5.24.3 , the lower bound passes to the limit, so $h\leq a\preceq \varphi $, and upward stability gives $a\in \mathcal E_\varphi $. Start with any subsequence and extract a further one along which the integrals in the hypothesis are at most $2^{-j}$ and $a_ j\to a$ almost everywhere for smooth volume. The finite rooftops \[  p_{j,N}=P_\theta (a_ j,\ldots ,a_ N)  \] are not identically $-\infty $ because $h$ is a competitor. Partitioning their contact sets according to the first obstacle touched gives \[  \int _ X\min (1,|p_{j,N}-a|)\mathrm{e}^{\lambda a}\, \mu _{p_{j,N}} \leq \sum _{k=j}^ N\int _ X|a_ k-a|\mathrm{e}^{\lambda a}\, \mu _{a_ k} \leq 2^{1-j}.  \] No relative-class assertion about these finite rooftops is needed. Their decreasing limits $p_ j=P_\theta (\inf _{k\geq j}a_ k)$ are at least $h$, and the almost-everywhere convergence gives $p_ j\leq a$. Hence the $p_ j$ and their increasing regularized limit $p$ lie in $\mathcal E_\varphi $. The limits in $N$ and then in $j$ hold in capacity by lemma 5.29.19 , since $h$ is a common lower bound. Apply the weighted lower semicontinuity lemma 13.14.8 twice, to the bounded weights $\min (1,|p_{j,N}-a|)\mathrm{e}^{\lambda a}$ and their limits. These weights converge in capacity: discard deep sublevel sets of $h$ and $a$, and use continuity on the remaining finite ranges. We obtain \[  \int _ X\min (1,|p-a|)\mathrm{e}^{\lambda a}\, \mu _ p=0.  \] The exponential is positive off a pluripolar set, which $\mu _ p$ does not charge. Hence $\mu _ p(\{ p<a\} )=0$, and zero domination gives $p=a$. The upper envelopes $(\sup _{k\geq j}a_ k)^*$ decrease to $a$, and squeezing proves convergence in capacity along this subsequence. Since the initial subsequence was arbitrary, the convergence holds for the original sequence. $\square$

title: 10.31.37 Ordinary types and bounded carriers
text:
We first solve the weighted addition equation when one input has the ordinary type of $\varphi $, or a measure dominated by the Monge–Ampère measure of a bounded potential. In both cases first moments control the rooftops of the approximating solutions, and these rooftops give the common lower bound required by lemma 10.31.35 . The solution lies below both inputs, so its measure is finite. Theorem 10.31.38 . 9A4A36BF299F Let $u,v\in \mathcal E_\varphi $ and $\lambda >0$. Suppose either $v\sim \varphi $, or there are a Hermitian metric $\omega $, a bounded $\psi \in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\omega )$ and a finite constant $A>0$ such that \[  \mu _ v\leq A\, \mathrm{MA}_\omega (\psi ).  \] Then there is a unique $a\in \mathcal E_\varphi $ satisfying \[  \mu _ a=\mathrm{e}^{\lambda (a-u)}\mu _ u+\mathrm{e}^{\lambda (a-v)}\mu _ v.  \] It satisfies $a\leq \min (u,v)$, and hence $\mu _ a\leq \mu _ u+\mu _ v$. If both $u,v\sim \varphi $, then also $a\sim \varphi $. Proof. The proof has four steps: two inputs of minimal singularity type, two inputs of the ordinary type of $\varphi $, one input of that type, and finally an input with a bounded carrier measure. It suffices to prove the result for $\lambda =1$. Indeed, replace $(	heta ,\varphi ,u,v)$ by $(\lambda 	heta ,\lambda \varphi ,\lambda u,\lambda v)$: envelopes and relative classes scale with the potentials, volumes and Monge–Ampère measures scale by $\lambda ^ n$, and a bounded-carrier domination remains one after changing its constant. Dividing the resulting solution by $\lambda $ gives the desired equation. Similarly, a common downward translation of $u$, $v$ and the solution allows us to assume $u,v\leq \varphi \leq 0$; by the envelope identity, these inequalities hold after a sufficiently large common translation. We restore the translation at the end. Step 1: inputs of minimal singularity type. First take $\varphi =V$ and $u,v\sim V$. Truncating only the weights, define the finite nonzero measures \[  	au _ j=\mathrm{e}^{-\max (u,-j)}\mu _ u+\mathrm{e}^{-\max (v,-j)}\mu _ v.  \] The functions $\max (u,-j)$ need not be $	heta $-plurisubharmonic; they occur only as weights. Theorem 10.31.22 gives $a_ j\in \mathcal E_ V$ with $\mu _{a_ j}=\mathrm{e}^{a_ j}	au _ j$. Choose $D\geq 	frac 12\| u-v\| _\infty +n\log 2$, where the difference is taken off the common poles, and put $w=(u+v)/2-D$. Positivity of mixed products gives \[  \mu _ w\geq 2^{-n}(\mu _ u+\mu _ v)\geq \mathrm{e}^ w	au _ j.  \] Exponential order in $\mathcal E_ V$ (corollary 13.19.3 ) gives $a_ j\geq w$. Since $	au _ j$ increases with $j$, the same order shows that $a_ j$ decreases. The envelope identity gives $a_1\leq V+\sup _ Xa_1$, so $a_1\sim V$ by the lower bound $w$. Consequently \[  \mu _{a_ j} \leq \mathrm{e}^{a_1-u}\mu _ u+\mathrm{e}^{a_1-v}\mu _ v \leq C(\mu _ u+\mu _ v).  \] The decreasing limit $a\geq w$ is not identically $-\infty $ and has the ordinary type of $V$. Fixed-dominator continuity (theorem 10.31.5 ) gives weak convergence of the left-hand sides, and the right-hand sides converge in total variation by dominated convergence with respect to $\mu _ u+\mu _ v$. Therefore \[  \mu _ a=\mathrm{e}^{a-u}\mu _ u+\mathrm{e}^{a-v}\mu _ v.  \] Comparing this equation with each input measure, exponential order now gives $a\leq u,v$. This comparison uses the limiting equation; the truncated weights alone would not give it. Step 2: two inputs of the ordinary type of $\varphi $. Suppose $u,v\sim \varphi $, and put $u_ j=\max (u,V-j)$ and $v_ j=\max (v,V-j)$. Step 1 gives solutions $a_ j\sim V$ with \[  \mu _{a_ j}=\mathrm{e}^{a_ j-u_ j}\mu _{u_ j}+\mathrm{e}^{a_ j-v_ j}\mu _{v_ j}, \qquad a_ j\leq \min (u_ j,v_ j).  \] The differences $u_ j-v_ j$ satisfy the same uniform bound as $u-v$. With $D$ as above, $w_ j=(u_ j+v_ j)/2-D$ satisfies the reverse inequality for this equation, and exponential order gives \[  (u+v)/2-D\leq w_ j\leq a_ j\leq \min (u_ j,v_ j).  \] The fixed lower bound $w=(u+v)/2-D$ has the ordinary type of $\varphi $, and hence lies in $\mathcal E_\varphi $. Extract an $L^1$ limit $a
ot\equiv -\infty $; it satisfies $w\leq a\leq \min (u,v)$, so $a\sim \varphi $. The input masses are at most $M_ V$. Lemma 10.31.35 , with $\sigma =V$ and lower bound $h=w$, proves convergence in capacity and the equation. The lemma applies although the approximating solutions have the type of $V$ and the limit has the type of $\varphi $. Step 3: one input of the ordinary type of $\varphi $. Now let $u\in \mathcal E_\varphi $ and $v\sim \varphi $, and set $u_ j=\max (u,\varphi -j)$. Step 2 gives $a_ j\sim \varphi $ with \[  \mu _{a_ j}=\mathrm{e}^{a_ j-u_ j}\mu _{u_ j}+\mathrm{e}^{a_ j-v}\mu _ v, \qquad a_ j\leq \min (u_ j,v).  \] We construct a common lower bound in $\mathcal E_\varphi $. Put $\delta =n\log 2>0$ and \[  s_ j=Q_2(a_ j,u_ j)\in \mathcal E_\varphi , \qquad C_ j=\{ s_ j+u_ j=2a_ j\} .  \] By stretching and contact, $s_ j\leq a_ j$ and 8E63C401924F 10.31.39  egin{equation}  2^{-n}\mu _{s_ j}+2^{-n}\mathbf1_{C_ j}\mu _{u_ j} \leq \mathbf1_{C_ j}\mu _{a_ j}. \end{equation} On $D_ j=\{ s_ j\leq u-2\delta \} $, contact implies $a_ j\leq u_ j-\delta $. Since $\mathrm{e}^{-\delta }=2^{-n}$, the $\mu _{u_ j}$ terms cancel in ( 10.31.39 ). Also $v\geq \varphi -C\geq u_ j-C$ for a fixed constant $C$. Hence AFD55911EAC6 10.31.40  egin{equation}  \mathbf1_{D_ j}\mu _{s_ j} \leq 2^ n \mathrm{e}^ C\mathbf1_{D_ j\cap C_ j} \mathrm{e}^{(s_ j-u_ j)/2}\mu _ v. \end{equation} All measures being subtracted here are finite. For $N\geq 1$ form the finite rooftops \[  R_ N=P_	heta (s_1,\ldots ,s_ N),\qquad q_ N=P_	heta (u,R_ N).  \] They belong to $\mathcal E_\varphi $ by the finite-rooftop proposition. On the set $\{ R_ N\leq u-2\delta \} $, partition the contact set according to the first index $i$ with $R_ N=s_ i$. Since $u_ i\geq u_ N$, ( 10.31.40 ) gives \[  \mathbf1_{\{ R_ N\leq u-2\delta \} }\mu _{R_ N} \leq 2^ n \mathrm{e}^ C \mathrm{e}^{(R_ N-u_ N)/2}\mu _ v.  \] The contact pieces are disjoint, so there is no factor $N$. On $\{ q_ N\leq u-2\delta \} $ only the contact part $q_ N=R_ N$ contributes. Since $u\leq u_ N$ and $t \mathrm{e}^{-t/2}\leq 2/\mathrm{e}$ for $t\geq 0$, we obtain \[  \int _ X(u-q_ N)\, \mu _{q_ N} \leq 2\delta M+2^{n+1}\mathrm{e}^{C-1}\mu _ v(X).  \] The first term bounds the contribution of the complementary set, including any contact with $u$. The first-moment criterion proposition 10.31.8 , with fixed reference $u$, implies that the decreasing sequence $q_ N$ has a limit $h\in \mathcal E_\varphi $, not identically $-\infty $. For each fixed $j$ and every $N\geq j$, we have $q_ N\leq s_ j\leq a_ j$, so $h\leq a_ j$ for every $j$. The $a_ j$ now have a subsequence converging in $L^1$ to a limit not identically $-\infty $, bounded above by $u$ and $v$. Lemma 10.31.35 , with reference $\varphi $, fixed second input $v$ and common lower bound $h$, proves the required equation in $\mathcal E_\varphi $; here the input masses are at most $M$. Step 4: a bounded carrier measure for the second input. Finally let $u,v\in \mathcal E_\varphi $ and $\mu _ v\leq A
u $, with $
u =\mathrm{MA}_\omega (\psi )$ and $\psi $ bounded. Again put $u_ j=\max (u,\varphi -j)$. By Step 3, applied with the inputs interchanged, there are $a_ j\in \mathcal E_\varphi $ satisfying the same equations and bounds as in Step 3. Let $r=P_	heta (u,v)\in \mathcal E_\varphi $. On $\{ a_ j<r\} $ one has $r\leq u_ j,v$, so the inequality $t \mathrm{e}^{-t}\leq 1/\mathrm{e}$ gives \[  \int _ X(r-a_ j)_+\, \mu _{a_ j} \leq \mathrm{e}^{-1} igl (\mu _{u_ j}(X)+\mu _ v(X) igr )\leq 2M/\mathrm{e}.  \] Since $a_ j\leq \varphi $, the one-sided first-moment criterion gives a uniform lower bound for $\sup _ Xa_ j$. By lemma 5.44.10 , \[  \sup _{\substack {z\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,	heta )\ \sup _ Xz=0}} \int _ X(-z)\, \mathrm{d}
u <\infty .  \] Applying this to $a_ j-\sup _ Xa_ j$ and using the lower bound for the suprema, we obtain 146C9C3A2FCA 10.31.41  egin{equation}  \sup _ j\int _ X(u_ j-a_ j)\, \mu _ v \leq \sup _ j\int _ X(-a_ j)\, \mu _ v<\infty . \end{equation} Keep $s_ j=Q_2(a_ j,u_ j)$, $C_ j$ and $D_ j$ from Step 3. The same cancellation in ( 10.31.39 ), now using only $a_ j\leq v$, gives \[  \mathbf1_{D_ j}\mu _{s_ j} \leq 2^ n\mathbf1_{D_ j\cap C_ j}\mathrm{e}^{a_ j-v}\mu _ v \leq 2^ n\mu _ v.  \] Take one additional rooftop, \[  q_ j=P_	heta (s_ j,u-2\delta )\in \mathcal E_\varphi .  \] On its contact set with $u-2\delta $ its measure is at most $\mu _ u$; on its other contact part, where $q_ j=s_ j\leq u-2\delta $, the preceding inequality applies. Thus A2C109F52CDC 10.31.42  egin{equation}  \mu _{q_ j}\leq \mu _ u+2^ n\mu _ v. \end{equation} Moreover the integrand $u-2\delta -q_ j$ vanishes on the first contact part. On the other part, the measure is carried by $C_ j$, where $u_ j-s_ j=2(u_ j-a_ j)$. Therefore \[  \int _ X(u-2\delta -q_ j)\, \mu _{q_ j} \leq 2^{n+1}\int _ X(u_ j-a_ j)\, \mu _ v,  \] which is uniformly bounded by ( 10.31.41 ). The first-moment criterion with reference $u-2\delta $ prevents collapse of the $q_ j$. Extract $L^1$ limits of the $a_ j$ and of the $q_ j$, not identically $-\infty $. The fixed-dominator theorem applies to ( 10.31.42 ) and, after a further extraction, gives \[  h=P_	heta \left(\inf _ jq_ jight)\in \mathcal E_\varphi .  \] Since $q_ j\leq s_ j\leq a_ j$, this is a common lower bound for the extracted solutions, and lemma 10.31.35 gives the equation. Its truncation levels are the original indices of the retained subsequence. In every step the solution lies below $u$ and $v$, so its measure is bounded by $\mu _ u+\mu _ v$. Two solutions have the same exponentially weighted measure, so corollary 13.19.3 , applied in both directions, gives uniqueness, even when that weighted measure has infinite mass. Restoring the common translation and the exponent finishes the proof. $\square$

title: 10.31.48 Arbitrary weighted sums
text: With existence for general measures available, weighted addition extends to arbitrary $u,v\in \mathcal E_\varphi $. Truncating the exponential weights gives finite data, which theorem 10.31.44 solves. A first-moment estimate prevents collapse of these solutions, and a rooftop involving their limit localizes the equation before the limit can be compared with the inputs. Theorem 10.31.49 . 9A2FDB1A65B5 For every $u,v\in \mathcal E_\varphi $ and $\lambda >0$, there is a unique $a\in \mathcal E_\varphi $ satisfying \[  \mu _ a=\mathrm{e}^{\lambda (a-u)}\mu _ u+\mathrm{e}^{\lambda (a-v)}\mu _ v.  \] Moreover $a\leq \min (u,v)$ and $\mu _ a\leq \mu _ u+\mu _ v$. Proof. By the scaling used in theorem 10.31.38 , it suffices to take $\lambda =1$. For positive integers $j$, let \[  \tau _ j=\mathrm{e}^{-\max (u,-j)}\mu _ u+\mathrm{e}^{-\max (v,-j)}\mu _ v.  \] These are nonzero finite non-pluripolar measures, and they increase with $j$. Only the weights are truncated; the functions $\max (u,-j)$ and $\max (v,-j)$ need not be $\theta $-plurisubharmonic. Theorem 10.31.44 gives $a_ j\in \mathcal E_\varphi $ with $\mu _{a_ j}=\mathrm{e}^{a_ j}\tau _ j$. Since $\tau _ j$ increases, exponential order implies that $a_ j$ decreases. Set $r=P_\theta (u,v)\in \mathcal E_\varphi $. On $\{ a_ j<r\} $, one has $r\leq u,v$ and \[  (r-a_ j)\mathrm{e}^{a_ j-\max (u,-j)}\leq (r-a_ j)\mathrm{e}^{a_ j-r}\leq \mathrm{e}^{-1},  \] with the same inequality for $v$. Consequently \[  \int _ X(r-a_ j)_+\, \mu _{a_ j} \leq \mathrm{e}^{-1}\bigl (\mu _ u(X)+\mu _ v(X)\bigr ).  \] Also $a_ j\leq a_1\leq \varphi +\sup _ Xa_1$. The one-sided first-moment criterion of proposition 10.31.8 , with fixed reference $r$, bounds $\sup _ Xa_ j$ from below. Thus the decreasing sequence has an $L^1$ limit $a\not\equiv -\infty $, and the same criterion puts $a$ in $\mathcal E_\varphi $. We identify the equation before comparing $a$ with the inputs. The rooftop \[  q=P_\theta (a,u,v)\in \mathcal E_\varphi  \] lies below $a_ j$, $a$, $u$ and $v$. For $T>0$, let $\chi _ T=g_ T(q)$, with $g_ T$ as in the proof of lemma 10.31.35 : a continuous nondecreasing cutoff that vanishes where $q\leq -2T$, equals one where $q\geq -T$, and increases to one off the pole set of $q$ as $T\to \infty $. On $\{ \chi _ T>0\} $ both inputs exceed $-2T$. Hence, for $j>2T$, 9B190A9E8A47 10.31.50 \begin{equation}  \chi _ T\mu _{a_ j} =\chi _ T \mathrm{e}^{a_ j}(\mathrm{e}^{-u}\mu _ u+\mathrm{e}^{-v}\mu _ v). \end{equation} The factors $\chi _ T\mathrm{e}^{-u}$ and $\chi _ T\mathrm{e}^{-v}$ are bounded by $\mathrm{e}^{2T}$. Since $a_ j\downarrow a$ and $a_ j\leq \sup _ Xa_1$, dominated convergence against the fixed measure $\mu _ u+\mu _ v$ gives convergence in total variation of the right-hand sides to the corresponding expression with $a$. For the left-hand side, $a_ j\to a$ in capacity by lemma 5.29.19 . Choose a Hermitian form $\Omega \geq \theta $, and replace $a_ j$ by $b_ j=\max (a_ j,-2T)$ before forming bounded products. The $b_ j$ are uniformly bounded $\Omega $-plurisubharmonic functions converging in capacity. The expansion \[  (\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}b_ j)^ n =\sum _{k=0}^ n\binom nk(\Omega +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}b_ j)^ k \wedge (\theta -\Omega )^{n-k}  \] and bounded capacity continuity apply against the fixed quasi-continuous weight $\chi _ T$. Where $\chi _ T\ne 0$ no potential is truncated, so locality gives convergence to $\chi _ T\mu _ a$. In this way the possibly signed bounded product is handled before the cutoff is inserted. Thus ( 10.31.50 ) holds in the limit. Let $T\to \infty $. Both sides ignore the poles of $q$, so monotone convergence gives \[  \mu _ a=\mathrm{e}^{a-u}\mu _ u+\mathrm{e}^{a-v}\mu _ v.  \] Since $a\in \mathcal E_\varphi $, this also shows that the weighted right-hand side is finite. For $\varepsilon >0$, the equation implies \[  \mathbf1_{\{ u<a-\varepsilon \} }\mu _ u \leq \mathrm{e}^{-\varepsilon }\mathbf1_{\{ u<a-\varepsilon \} }\mu _ a.  \] Strict domination, theorem 13.19.1 , gives $u\geq a-\varepsilon $, and letting $\varepsilon \downarrow 0$ gives $u\geq a$. Similarly $v\geq a$, so $\mu _ a\leq \mu _ u+\mu _ v$. Two solutions have the same exponentially weighted measure, so corollary 13.19.3 , applied in both directions, gives uniqueness. $\square$ Corollary 10.31.51 . DE6440832625 For fixed $\lambda >0$, write $u\star _\lambda v$ for the solution $a$ in the theorem. This operation on $\mathcal E_\varphi $ is commutative and associative, and, for $c\in \mathbb R$, \[  (u+c)\star _\lambda (v+c)=(u\star _\lambda v)+c, \qquad u\star _\lambda u=u-\lambda ^{-1}\log 2.  \] Proof. Put $F_\lambda (u)=\mathrm{e}^{-\lambda u}\mu _ u$, with zero mass on the poles. The theorem says that $F_\lambda (u\star _\lambda v)=F_\lambda (u)+F_\lambda (v)$. By corollary 13.19.3 , the map $F_\lambda $ is injective on $\mathcal E_\varphi $. Commutativity and associativity therefore follow from those of addition of positive measures, including measures of infinite total mass. Finally, $F_\lambda (u+c)=\mathrm{e}^{-\lambda c}F_\lambda (u)$, which together with injectivity gives both identities. $\square$

title: 10.31.52 Relative boundedness for $L^ p$ data
text: If the datum has finite moments of sufficiently high order against normalized $\theta $-plurisubharmonic functions, every normalized $u\in \mathcal E_\varphi $ whose measure is dominated by the datum differs from $\varphi $ by a bounded function. We work directly with $u\in \mathcal E_\varphi $: truncating $u$ against $\varphi -j$ would introduce a contact measure that need not be controlled by the datum. Envelopes with concave obstacles, as in lemma 10.31.14 , keep this domination and give a differential inequality for the distribution of $\varphi -u$. Lemma 10.31.53 . F816A9EF0F9D Let $u\in \mathcal E_\varphi $ with $u\leq \varphi $, and let $\chi :\mathbb R_{\leq 0}\to \mathbb R_{\leq 0}$ be increasing and concave, with $\chi (0)=0$. Suppose that $\chi $ is $C^{1,1}$ on compact intervals and that, for a finite constant $L\geq 1$, \[  1\leq \chi '\leq L.  \] Then the envelope \[  p=P_\theta (\varphi +\chi (u-\varphi ))  \] belongs to $\mathcal E_\varphi $, and \[  \mu _ p\leq \mathbf1_{\{ p=\varphi +\chi (u-\varphi )\} } \chi '(u-\varphi )^ n\mu _ u.  \] Here the obstacle and the contact set are defined off the pluripolar set where $u-\varphi $ is undefined, which all these measures ignore. Proof. For $t\leq 0$, the bounds on $\chi '$ give $Lt\leq \chi (t)\leq t$. Thus \[  Q_ L(u,\varphi )\leq p\leq u\leq \varphi .  \] The lower potential belongs to $\mathcal E_\varphi $ by lemma 16.28.63 , so $p$ is not identically $-\infty $ and belongs to $\mathcal E_\varphi $ by upward stability. The obstacle is finite and quasi-continuous off the poles, so the contact theorem theorem 15.8.6 applies. Let $\tau =\chi ^{-1}$. It is convex, with $L^{-1}\leq \tau '\leq 1$. We justify the transformation \[  w=\varphi +\tau (p-\varphi )  \] without assuming that $\varphi $ is locally bounded on some open set. On a coordinate ball choose a smooth function $q$ with $\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}q\geq 0$. The functions \[  p_ m=\max (p,q-m),\qquad \varphi _ m=\max (\varphi ,q-m)  \] are locally bounded $\theta $-plurisubharmonic functions on the ball, and $p_ m\leq \varphi _ m$. Lemma 5.28.13 applies to $w_ m=\varphi _ m+\tau (p_ m-\varphi _ m)$ and gives \[  \theta _{w_ m}\geq 0,\qquad \mu _{w_ m}\geq \tau '(p_ m-\varphi _ m)^ n\mu _{p_ m}.  \] The function $(s,t)\mapsto t+\tau (s-t)$ on $\{ s\leq t\} $ is nondecreasing in each variable. Consequently $w_ m$ decreases as $m$ increases. Since $p\leq p_ m\leq w_ m\leq \varphi _ m$, the limit is not identically $-\infty $ on the ball. Off the poles it equals $w$. The local limits therefore agree on overlaps after regularization and define a global $\theta $-plurisubharmonic function. On $D_ m=\{ p>q-m\} $, neither $p$ nor $\varphi $ is truncated. Thus $w_ m=w$ there, and plurifine locality transfers the product inequality to $D_ m$. These sets exhaust the complement of the poles of $p$ in the ball. Since all products ignore the discarded pluripolar set, \[  \mu _ w\geq \tau '(p-\varphi )^ n\mu _ p.  \] The obstacle bound $p\leq \varphi +\chi (u-\varphi )$ gives $w\leq u$, with equality on the contact set of $p$. Ordered contact, the identity $\tau '(p-\varphi )=1/\chi '(u-\varphi )$ on that set, and contact support of $\mu _ p$ prove the assertion. $\square$ Proposition 10.31.54 . 36BCEF7C4255 Let $\mu $ be a finite non-pluripolar measure. Suppose that, for some real $m>2n+1$, \[  A_ m:=\sup _{\substack {v\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )\\ \sup _ Xv=0}} \int _ X(-v)^ m\, \mathrm{d}\mu <\infty .  \] There is a finite constant $C$, depending only on $n,\ell ,M,m,\mu (X)$ and $A_ m$, such that every $u\in \mathcal E_\varphi $ with $\sup _ Xu=0$ and $\mu _ u\leq \mu $ satisfies \[  \varphi -C\leq u\leq \varphi .  \] Proof. As in proposition 10.31.15 , we build a concave weight from the distribution of $\varphi -u$ and apply the preceding lemma. The moment bound on $\mu $ now yields a differential inequality for this weight, which bounds the depth of $\varphi -u$ under $\mu _ u$. The envelope identity gives $u\leq \varphi \leq 0$. Put $x=\varphi -u$, defined off the poles, and $N=2n+1$. Since $x\leq -u$ and $\mu _ u\leq \mu $, Hölder's inequality gives the uniform first-moment bound \[  B:=\int _ Xx\, \mu _ u \leq \int _ X(-u)\, \mathrm{d}\mu \leq \mu (X)^{1-1/m}A_ m^{1/m}=:A_1.  \] Let $H(t)=\mu _ u(\{ x>t\} )$ and $T=\sup \{ t\geq 0:H(t)>0\} $, with $T=0$ if this set is empty; at this point $T$ may be infinite. If $T<\infty $, zero domination applied to $u$ and $\varphi -t$ for $t>T$ gives $u\geq \varphi -T$. It is therefore enough to bound $T$. We may assume $T>1$, and we choose any $S$ with $1<S<T$. Define, for $t\geq 0$, \[  g(t)= \begin{cases}  ((1+t)^{3/2}H(t))^{-1},& 0\leq t\leq S,\\  (1+t)^{-3/2},& t>S, \end{cases} \qquad F(t)=1+\int _0^ t g(s)\, \mathrm{d}s,  \] and set $W(t)=\int _0^ t F(s)^{1/N}\, \mathrm{d}s$ and $\chi (-t)=-W(t)$. Since $H(S)>0$, $F$ is bounded on the whole half-line, although its bound may depend on $S$ and $u$. It is locally Lipschitz and nondecreasing. Hence $\chi $ has bounded derivative, is increasing and concave, and satisfies the hypotheses of the preceding lemma. Also $W(t)\geq t$ and $W(t)\leq tF(t)^{1/N}$. Since $H(t)\leq M$, Tonelli's theorem gives a bound independent of $S$ and $u$: \[  \int _ X F(x)\, \mu _ u =\mu _ u(X)+\int _0^\infty g(t)H(t)\, \mathrm{d}t \leq 3\max (1,M)=:K.  \] Let $p=P_\theta (\varphi -W(x))\in \mathcal E_\varphi $, the envelope of the preceding lemma for this $\chi $. On its contact set the lemma bounds its measure by $F(x)^{n/N}\mu _ u$. Hence, using $N=2n+1$ and the Cauchy–Schwarz inequality, \[  \begin{split}  \int _ X(\varphi -p)^{1/2}\, \mu _ p & \leq \int _ X x^{1/2}F(x)^{(n+1/2)/N}\, \mu _ u\\ & \leq \left(\int _ Xx\, \mu _ u\right)^{1/2} \left(\int _ XF(x)\, \mu _ u\right)^{1/2} \leq \sqrt{KB}. \end{split}  \] The identity $P_\theta [p]=\varphi $ implies $p-\sup _ Xp\leq \varphi $. Since $p\leq \varphi \leq 0$ and $\mu _ p(X)\geq \ell $, the last integral is at least $\ell \sqrt{-\sup _ Xp}$. Consequently \[  0\leq -\sup _ Xp\leq KA_1/\ell ^2=:D.  \] Using $W(x)\leq \varphi -p\leq -p$, and applying the moment hypothesis to $p-\sup _ Xp$, we obtain 9E93E3C5CAED 10.31.55 \begin{equation}  \int _ XW(x)^ m\, \mathrm{d}\mu \leq 2^{m-1}\bigl (A_ m+D^ m\mu (X)\bigr )<C_0, \end{equation} where we choose $C_0=1+2^{m-1}(A_ m+D^ m\mu (X))$. This constant is independent of $S$ and $u$. For $0<t\leq S$, Chebyshev's inequality and $\mu _ u\leq \mu $ give \[  H(t)\leq C_0W(t)^{-m}, \qquad F'(t)\geq \frac{W(t)^ m}{C_0(1+t)^{3/2}} \quad \text{for almost every }t.  \] Since $W'=F^{1/N}$, the derivative of $(W')^{N+1}$ is at least \[  \frac{N+1}{NC_0}\,  \frac{W^ mW'}{(1+t)^{3/2}}.  \] All functions being differentiated are absolutely continuous on compact intervals. Integrating from $0$ to $t$ and using $W(0)=0$ gives \[  (W'(t))^{N+1} \geq \frac{N+1}{NC_0(m+1)} \frac{W(t)^{m+1}}{(1+t)^{3/2}}.  \] In particular \[  W'(t)\geq c_0(1+t)^{-\gamma }W(t)^\kappa , \quad \gamma =\frac{3}{2(N+1)}<1,\quad \kappa =\frac{m+1}{N+1}>1,  \] with $c_0>0$ independent of $S$ and $u$. Integrating the derivative of $W^{1-\kappa }$ over $[1,S]$ yields \[  (\kappa -1)c_0\int _1^ S(1+t)^{-\gamma }\, \mathrm{d}t \leq W(1)^{1-\kappa }-W(S)^{1-\kappa }\leq 1,  \] because $W(1)\geq 1$. Since the integral on the left diverges as $S\to \infty $, every $S<T$ is bounded by a constant independent of $S$ and $u$, and hence so is $T$. The zero-domination argument at the beginning of the proof now gives $u\geq \varphi -C$. The case $T\leq 1$, which includes $B=0$, was covered there as well. $\square$ Corollary 10.31.56 . B2E2FCD34986 Let $0\leq f\in L^ p(X,\mathrm{d}V)$, with $p>1$ and $\int _ Xf\, \mathrm{d}V>0$. For $\lambda >0$, the solution in theorem 10.31.44 of \[  \mathrm{MA}_\theta (u)=\mathrm{e}^{\lambda u}f\, \mathrm{d}V  \] satisfies $u\sim \varphi $. Every normalized solution in $\mathcal E_\varphi $ of \[  \mathrm{MA}_\theta (u)=cf\, \mathrm{d}V,\qquad c>0,  \] also satisfies $u\sim \varphi $. In particular, both existence statements hold in the ordinary singularity type of $\varphi $. Proof. Lemma 5.26.2 , applied in a Hermitian background dominating $\theta $, gives uniform moments of every finite order against $\mathrm{d}V$ for normalized $\theta $-plurisubharmonic functions. Hölder's inequality therefore implies, for every finite $m$, \[  \sup _{\substack {v\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )\\ \sup _ Xv=0}} \int _ X(-v)^ m f\, \mathrm{d}V<\infty .  \] Choose $m>2n+1$. For the solution of the exponential equation, set $S=\sup _ Xu$ and $v=u-S$. Then $v\in \mathcal E_\varphi $, $\sup _ Xv=0$, and \[  \mu _ v=\mathrm{e}^{\lambda u}f\, \mathrm{d}V \leq \mathrm{e}^{\lambda S}f\, \mathrm{d}V.  \] The preceding proposition, applied to this fixed dominating measure, shows that $v$, and hence $u$, has the ordinary type of $\varphi $. For the normalized equation, apply the proposition to the measure $cf\, \mathrm{d}V$. $\square$

title: Lemma 10.31.53
text: Lemma 10.31.53 . F816A9EF0F9D Let $u\in \mathcal E_\varphi $ with $u\leq \varphi $, and let $\chi :\mathbb R_{\leq 0}\to \mathbb R_{\leq 0}$ be increasing and concave, with $\chi (0)=0$. Suppose that $\chi $ is $C^{1,1}$ on compact intervals and that, for a finite constant $L\geq 1$, \[  1\leq \chi '\leq L.  \] Then the envelope \[  p=P_\theta (\varphi +\chi (u-\varphi ))  \] belongs to $\mathcal E_\varphi $, and \[  \mu _ p\leq \mathbf1_{\{ p=\varphi +\chi (u-\varphi )\} } \chi '(u-\varphi )^ n\mu _ u.  \] Here the obstacle and the contact set are defined off the pluripolar set where $u-\varphi $ is undefined, which all these measures ignore. Proof. For $t\leq 0$, the bounds on $\chi '$ give $Lt\leq \chi (t)\leq t$. Thus \[  Q_ L(u,\varphi )\leq p\leq u\leq \varphi .  \] The lower potential belongs to $\mathcal E_\varphi $ by lemma 16.28.63 , so $p$ is not identically $-\infty $ and belongs to $\mathcal E_\varphi $ by upward stability. The obstacle is finite and quasi-continuous off the poles, so the contact theorem theorem 15.8.6 applies. Let $\tau =\chi ^{-1}$. It is convex, with $L^{-1}\leq \tau '\leq 1$. We justify the transformation \[  w=\varphi +\tau (p-\varphi )  \] without assuming that $\varphi $ is locally bounded on some open set. On a coordinate ball choose a smooth function $q$ with $\theta +\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm{c}}q\geq 0$. The functions \[  p_ m=\max (p,q-m),\qquad \varphi _ m=\max (\varphi ,q-m)  \] are locally bounded $\theta $-plurisubharmonic functions on the ball, and $p_ m\leq \varphi _ m$. Lemma 5.28.13 applies to $w_ m=\varphi _ m+\tau (p_ m-\varphi _ m)$ and gives \[  \theta _{w_ m}\geq 0,\qquad \mu _{w_ m}\geq \tau '(p_ m-\varphi _ m)^ n\mu _{p_ m}.  \] The function $(s,t)\mapsto t+\tau (s-t)$ on $\{ s\leq t\} $ is nondecreasing in each variable. Consequently $w_ m$ decreases as $m$ increases. Since $p\leq p_ m\leq w_ m\leq \varphi _ m$, the limit is not identically $-\infty $ on the ball. Off the poles it equals $w$. The local limits therefore agree on overlaps after regularization and define a global $\theta $-plurisubharmonic function. On $D_ m=\{ p>q-m\} $, neither $p$ nor $\varphi $ is truncated. Thus $w_ m=w$ there, and plurifine locality transfers the product inequality to $D_ m$. These sets exhaust the complement of the poles of $p$ in the ball. Since all products ignore the discarded pluripolar set, \[  \mu _ w\geq \tau '(p-\varphi )^ n\mu _ p.  \] The obstacle bound $p\leq \varphi +\chi (u-\varphi )$ gives $w\leq u$, with equality on the contact set of $p$. Ordered contact, the identity $\tau '(p-\varphi )=1/\chi '(u-\varphi )$ on that set, and contact support of $\mu _ p$ prove the assertion. $\square$

title: Proposition 10.31.54
text: Proposition 10.31.54 . 36BCEF7C4255 Let $\mu $ be a finite non-pluripolar measure. Suppose that, for some real $m>2n+1$, \[  A_ m:=\sup _{\substack {v\in \mathrm{PSH}(X,\theta )\\ \sup _ Xv=0}} \int _ X(-v)^ m\, \mathrm{d}\mu <\infty .  \] There is a finite constant $C$, depending only on $n,\ell ,M,m,\mu (X)$ and $A_ m$, such that every $u\in \mathcal E_\varphi $ with $\sup _ Xu=0$ and $\mu _ u\leq \mu $ satisfies \[  \varphi -C\leq u\leq \varphi .  \] Proof. As in proposition 10.31.15 , we build a concave weight from the distribution of $\varphi -u$ and apply the preceding lemma. The moment bound on $\mu $ now yields a differential inequality for this weight, which bounds the depth of $\varphi -u$ under $\mu _ u$. The envelope identity gives $u\leq \varphi \leq 0$. Put $x=\varphi -u$, defined off the poles, and $N=2n+1$. Since $x\leq -u$ and $\mu _ u\leq \mu $, Hölder's inequality gives the uniform first-moment bound \[  B:=\int _ Xx\, \mu _ u \leq \int _ X(-u)\, \mathrm{d}\mu \leq \mu (X)^{1-1/m}A_ m^{1/m}=:A_1.  \] Let $H(t)=\mu _ u(\{ x>t\} )$ and $T=\sup \{ t\geq 0:H(t)>0\} $, with $T=0$ if this set is empty; at this point $T$ may be infinite. If $T<\infty $, zero domination applied to $u$ and $\varphi -t$ for $t>T$ gives $u\geq \varphi -T$. It is therefore enough to bound $T$. We may assume $T>1$, and we choose any $S$ with $1<S<T$. Define, for $t\geq 0$, \[  g(t)= \begin{cases}  ((1+t)^{3/2}H(t))^{-1},& 0\leq t\leq S,\\  (1+t)^{-3/2},& t>S, \end{cases} \qquad F(t)=1+\int _0^ t g(s)\, \mathrm{d}s,  \] and set $W(t)=\int _0^ t F(s)^{1/N}\, \mathrm{d}s$ and $\chi (-t)=-W(t)$. Since $H(S)>0$, $F$ is bounded on the whole half-line, although its bound may depend on $S$ and $u$. It is locally Lipschitz and nondecreasing. Hence $\chi $ has bounded derivative, is increasing and concave, and satisfies the hypotheses of the preceding lemma. Also $W(t)\geq t$ and $W(t)\leq tF(t)^{1/N}$. Since $H(t)\leq M$, Tonelli's theorem gives a bound independent of $S$ and $u$: \[  \int _ X F(x)\, \mu _ u =\mu _ u(X)+\int _0^\infty g(t)H(t)\, \mathrm{d}t \leq 3\max (1,M)=:K.  \] Let $p=P_\theta (\varphi -W(x))\in \mathcal E_\varphi $, the envelope of the preceding lemma for this $\chi $. On its contact set the lemma bounds its measure by $F(x)^{n/N}\mu _ u$. Hence, using $N=2n+1$ and the Cauchy–Schwarz inequality, \[  \begin{split}  \int _ X(\varphi -p)^{1/2}\, \mu _ p & \leq \int _ X x^{1/2}F(x)^{(n+1/2)/N}\, \mu _ u\\ & \leq \left(\int _ Xx\, \mu _ u\right)^{1/2} \left(\int _ XF(x)\, \mu _ u\right)^{1/2} \leq \sqrt{KB}. \end{split}  \] The identity $P_\theta [p]=\varphi $ implies $p-\sup _ Xp\leq \varphi $. Since $p\leq \varphi \leq 0$ and $\mu _ p(X)\geq \ell $, the last integral is at least $\ell \sqrt{-\sup _ Xp}$. Consequently \[  0\leq -\sup _ Xp\leq KA_1/\ell ^2=:D.  \] Using $W(x)\leq \varphi -p\leq -p$, and applying the moment hypothesis to $p-\sup _ Xp$, we obtain 9E93E3C5CAED 10.31.55 \begin{equation}  \int _ XW(x)^ m\, \mathrm{d}\mu \leq 2^{m-1}\bigl (A_ m+D^ m\mu (X)\bigr )<C_0, \end{equation} where we choose $C_0=1+2^{m-1}(A_ m+D^ m\mu (X))$. This constant is independent of $S$ and $u$. For $0<t\leq S$, Chebyshev's inequality and $\mu _ u\leq \mu $ give \[  H(t)\leq C_0W(t)^{-m}, \qquad F'(t)\geq \frac{W(t)^ m}{C_0(1+t)^{3/2}} \quad \text{for almost every }t.  \] Since $W'=F^{1/N}$, the derivative of $(W')^{N+1}$ is at least \[  \frac{N+1}{NC_0}\,  \frac{W^ mW'}{(1+t)^{3/2}}.  \] All functions being differentiated are absolutely continuous on compact intervals. Integrating from $0$ to $t$ and using $W(0)=0$ gives \[  (W'(t))^{N+1} \geq \frac{N+1}{NC_0(m+1)} \frac{W(t)^{m+1}}{(1+t)^{3/2}}.  \] In particular \[  W'(t)\geq c_0(1+t)^{-\gamma }W(t)^\kappa , \quad \gamma =\frac{3}{2(N+1)}<1,\quad \kappa =\frac{m+1}{N+1}>1,  \] with $c_0>0$ independent of $S$ and $u$. Integrating the derivative of $W^{1-\kappa }$ over $[1,S]$ yields \[  (\kappa -1)c_0\int _1^ S(1+t)^{-\gamma }\, \mathrm{d}t \leq W(1)^{1-\kappa }-W(S)^{1-\kappa }\leq 1,  \] because $W(1)\geq 1$. Since the integral on the left diverges as $S\to \infty $, every $S<T$ is bounded by a constant independent of $S$ and $u$, and hence so is $T$. The zero-domination argument at the beginning of the proof now gives $u\geq \varphi -C$. The case $T\leq 1$, which includes $B=0$, was covered there as well. $\square$
